text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.

- Low educational standards in Portugal slow down economic growth and productivity, a report from the European Commission says. It says Portuguese industry has not been sufficiently restructured and that salaries are comparatively low.

- Portugal and Spain increased trade with each other after joining the European Community in 1986. Since 1991, Spanish companies' share of the Portuguese market has risen by more than that of Portuguese companies in the Spanish market, partly because of the appreciation of the escudo.
- The Portuguese government will propose changes to the Common Agricultural Policy in which income support would depend on the number of farmers in a country.
- The Finance Ministry will invest some 2.5 billion escudos in a computer system to combat tax evasion.

- A programme to encourage activity by Portuguese companies abroad, which will be ready this summer, will make available 150 billion escudos to be used in investment projects and credits, according to Under-Secretary for Competition, Freire de Sousa.
- The Portuguese economy developed favourably in February, although private consumption fell, according to a report from the National Statistics Institute (INE).
- Francisco de Assis, leader of the ruling Socialist Party parlamentary group, said the opposition Social Democratic Party (PSD) should adopt a clearer position on regionalisation.

- Bagao Felix, former Bank of Portugal vice-governor, believes that Portugal should join the European single currency from the start because to postpone its entry would be harmful to the interests of the country.
